items.measurement_basis: EXECUTE lane-turn reliability: attempts BC1 and BC2 wedged (first file written, then no progress) and BC2 was terminated by the orchestrator on measurement. On the arm: the identity gate passed ONLY on BC3 (`required_arm == served_arm == opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `usage_receipt_ok: true`, rank 1). BC1's ATTEMPT-level attribution names the mandated arm (opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash) but BC1's own aggregate verdict is `ok:false / ERR_LANE_ALL_ROUTES_EXHAUSTED / usage_receipt_ok:false / served_arm:null`, so BC1 does NOT establish arm identity; BC2 has no receipt at all and establishes nothing about the arm, although it DID produce the effort test module before wedging (tests/test_lane_effort_enforcement.py, mtime 11:30:24, 26 s into its own window and inside no other attempt's), which BC3 reused unchanged and which is therefore credited to BC2. Both fields are printed side by side in README's lane table for exactly this reason. The remedy applied in-round was an EDIT-ONLY turn (BC3), which completed in 74 s. A lane that wedges twice on the same brief shape is a standing reliability caveat for future rounds.

reconciliation.what: the strict entry (maker EXECUTE, checker PLAN, distinct_required true) was REMOVED from sod_invariants.pairs. The overlap remains RECORDED here rather than refused, which is what the owner's own 2026-10-10 lane-route-slots declaration already says -- selection_semantics.sod is "NOT enforced; identity overlaps are recorded as facts only, not as refusals", and identity_overlaps_recorded_not_enforced lists this very identity.
reconciliation.why_not_a_model_change: PLAN's binding (opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash) is the owner's declared rank-1 DEFAULT for the PLAN lane; moving it would have been rework and would have displaced the owner's own pool declaration. The defect was the ENCODING, not the binding.
compensating_control: structural: PLAN and EXECUTE are both maker/executor routes and never check each other; the acceptance/verification route is the dedicated VERIFY_SECURITY lane (arm A), the only lane that checks another lane's artifacts.
artifact-level: every checker lane writes through the C1 verdict-artifact contract (write-first, shape-validated, updated_by_checker), so a checker cannot pass by omission.
per-card: the reasoning pin of the checking lane is recorded per card.
reconciliation.residual: with the model axis no longer enforced between the two maker/executor routes, the remaining separation between them is ROLE and ARTIFACT, not model identity. Recorded as an accepted risk, not as a passing invariant.
